en: O Blessed Lady, your beloved is the Supreme Person; the Lord of Serpents is your bed, seat, and vehicle; the Lord of Birds, whose soul is the Vedas, is your curtain that deludes the world;
the host of gods beginning with Brahmā, together with their consorts, is the multitude of your male and female servants; and your name is indeed "Śrī"—how, then, can we describe you?

O Sole Mistress of the worlds, beloved of the Lord of the worlds, I shall praise you—knowing your compassion for those who are self-controlled—with the confidence that "I am your servant" and "I have sought refuge in you," even though your lover, the Lord himself, is unable to measure your greatness, which is like his own self, boundless, eternal, and inherently favorable; for he too cannot fathom its limit. (YCs 2)

It is better that the three worlds, which were previously lost due to the lack of such [vision], are now protected by the nourishment of the nectar of your compassionate gaze, resulting in infinite prosperity;
for indeed, apart from the grace of the lotus-eyed one who is beloved to the heart, it is never possible for men to attain welfare on the paths of worldly existence, liberation, or Vaiṣṇavism.
That form of Hari which is the supreme Brahman, characterized by infinite and peaceful great majesty, is more dear to You than even that embodied Brahman;
and as for all those other forms assumed when You sport according to Your pleasure, they say they are all firmly embraced by Your own sovereign manifestations of form suited to each.
